summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of liver transplant for primary sclerosing cholangitis was admitted with a month-long history of fever, headaches, nausea, and abdominal pain. She was found to have severe neutropenia, likely due to medication effects from MMF and dapsone, with an initial concern for CMV viremia. Repeat testing showed undetectable CMV viral load, ruling out active infection. Dapsone was switched to atovaquone, MMF was temporarily held, and Neupogen was administered to support white blood cell recovery. A colonoscopy was performed due to concern for colitis, revealing a normal colon with negative biopsies for CMV. Her white count improved, and she remained afebrile. She was discharged home with resolved symptoms, resumed immunosuppression, and plans for outpatient follow-up including repeat colonoscopy for screening.
